newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall on election worries.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall on election worries.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted losses on Wednesday in late selling prompted by Turkish State Minister Abdullah Gul's remarks on early elections, brokers said.
Gul said his Welfare Party, the Islamist wing of the cabinet was prepared to call elections as a last resort but was reluctant to do so for fear of harming the economy.

The IMKB National-100 closed 18 points, or 1.16 percent lower at 1,530 after rebounding from a late low of 1,518. Volume firmed to 21.12 trillion lira ($161.5 million) from Tuesday's 17.07 trillion ($131 million) because of the late fluctuations.

"The market is highly susceptible to politics. The early election comments had a quite negative impact. It will remain indexed to politicians' statements tomorrow," said Korhan Biricik from Deha securities.
The market has been haunted by a liquidity shortage in recent days due to persisting political uncertainities and reluctance to buy ahead of an upcoming long holiday.

A religious holiday between April 17-21 will be followed by an official holiday on April 23. The government has declared April 22 holiday for state offices, but it is not yet known if the markets will be closed.
